title: API key reissue split-brain during zonal failover leads to transient org misbinding
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: During several customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments we observed transient authorization mismatches after API key reissue events that coincided with zone-level failovers. A subset of requests were accepted with a newly minted token but bound to the previous org mapping, causing intermittent cross-tenant responses or 401/403s depending on routing. The issue reproduced under load when the token reissue service and the zone leader election both acted without a global coordination step.
incident_summary: Multiple enterprise customers (2 Dedicated, 3 Private, and 1 Hosted) reported intermittent 401/403s and rare cross-organization data exposure during a maintenance window and an unrelated zonal outage. Impact lasted for ~18 minutes for most customers; one Dedicated customer experienced repeated failures during scaling operations and opened an escalation ticket. Support routed as P0 and we engaged on-call SRE and identity engineers.
timeline:
2026-03-05 02:10 UTC: Bulk key-roll job started in us-west-2
2026-03-05 02:12 UTC: Partial zone outage caused leader handoff in us-west-2a
2026-03-05 02:13-02:20 UTC: Token reissue service issued tokens concurrently in us-west-2a and us-west-2b without global coordination
2026-03-05 02:20 UTC: First customer reported 401s to support (ticket #CS-2241)
2026-03-05 02:28 UTC: Pager escalated to SRE and Identity on-call
2026-03-05 02:34 UTC: Mitigation deployed (short TTL, global validation gate)
2026-03-05 02:50 UTC: Normal traffic restored; post-incident analysis initiated
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Trigger a coordinated API key reissue for an org while simultaneously inducing a leader election in one availability zone.
2) Send concurrent live requests routed to different zones during the reissue window.
3) Observe that some requests accept the new token but validate against stale org mapping cached locally, leading to 403s or incorrect routing.
Repro is timing-sensitive; increasing request QPS and reducing reissue propagation delay makes it reliably reproducible in staging.
root_cause: A race between the token reissue flow and zone-local org mapping cache writes. When leader election promoted a new zone-local token-issuer, both the old and new issuers issued tokens for the same API key during a narrow window. Each zone wrote its own mapping into its local cache/fastpath without a global canonicalization step. Because requests are routed by zone affinity, some requests validated tokens against a divergent mapping and were mis-scoped. Additionally, the token reissue path did not include an idempotent issuance check or a write-through to the global org-mapping service, which allowed split-brain state to persist for the token TTL window.
fix:
1) Implemented a global issuance guard: token reissue now acquires a short-lived global lock (etcd-backed) for the API key during reissue.
2) Reworked issuance to be idempotent: issuers check a canonical issuance token in the global mapping before creating a new token.
3) Updated cache semantics: writes during reissue are write-through to global mapping and include a ‘version’ tag so zones can reconcile.
4) Reduced default reissued token propagation TTL and added an active validation step that asks a global validator when a token is seen for the first time in a zone.
5) Added end-to-end integration tests that simulate leader handoff during reissue and added a stress test in staging that runs nightly.
verification: Staging runs: 48-hour stress test with repeated leader elections and key roll events passed with zero mismatches. Canary rollout: deployed to 10% of traffic for 2 hours, then 50% for 4 hours with monitoring alerts looking for 5xx/403 spikes and cross-tenant hits; no regressions observed. Full rollout completed 2026-03-05 02:45 UTC. Post-deploy validation against customer traffic logs confirmed no further misbinding.
rollout_notes: Canary configuration: identity service runtime-1.23; global guard enabled via feature flag identity.reissue.global_guard = true. Rollout strategy: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 1 hour. Emergency rollback: set feature flag to false and temporarily increase token TTL to avoid flip-flopping during rollback. Rollout executed by on-call SRE with runbook: runbook/ID-REISSUE-001.
resolution_notes: Fix merged in identity@runtime-1.23. We validated with customers and reopened a support case with the most impacted Dedicated customer to perform a joint replay to confirm no residual effects. Long-term design changes include consolidating issuance into the global control-plane and exploring a single-source-of-truth for api-key metadata to prevent future zone-local divergence.
notes: Security reviewed the changes and confirmed no escalation of privileges during fix (sec ticket SEC-998).
